You are helping run CrosswordChat's daily "growth-extract" lesson-mining task (Claudinite framework). Your job is ONLY to research and report candidate lessons — do NOT write any files or make any edits.

Read this captured agent session log in full: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-CrosswordChat/f185c295-f140-5914-b64a-272487a91594/scratchpad/logs/2026-08-16T1452Z--issue-201--a0603cdf-f0fd-5c34-ade8-a21ca2c946a5.jsonl`

## What to look for (friction signals)

1. **Misunderstandings**: a clarifying round-trip, the user correcting an assumption ("no, I meant…"), the agent building the wrong thing and reworking it, an AskUserQuestion whose answer was an obvious default in hindsight.
2. **Suboptimal agent actions**: an approach taken then backtracked, redundant/repeated work, re-running a command that had already failed for a knowable reason, reaching for a heavy tool where a light one fit, reinventing something the codebase already provided, re-reading a just-written file to "verify", missing an existing convention corrected in review.
3. **Long wall-time waits**: independent operations run serially with no dependency, a padded fixed sleep, a process waited out after its result was already in hand, blind long polling, re-running an already-green check. Measure with REAL numbers from the log's own timestamps — compute time vs genuine idle waiting. Don't estimate.

## Bar for a candidate (be skeptical — most sessions yield nothing)

A signal only qualifies if it's durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one session — not a one-off, not a restatement of a generic truism, not something already implied by an existing rule. This repo ALREADY has two local packs capturing lessons — do NOT propose anything overlapping these (I'll paste their current content below; check against it before reporting anything):

### Existing browser-speech local pack covers:
- chrome.tts not exposed to content scripts (relay via cc-session port)
- self-echo is an app problem not a constraints problem (webkitSpeechRecognition owns its own capture, no MediaTrackConstraints hook); suppressLocalAudioPlayback/restrictOwnAudio are getDisplayMedia-only traps
- mic permission preflight: run even when already granted, retry once bare on constrained-call rejection
- endpointing pause-window tuning (1.2s too short, 1.8s right), interim results gated as "still speaking" signal only
- contextual biasing (SpeechRecognitionPhrase/processLocally) is on-device-only, probe once/memoize, accept only literal 'available', try/catch fallback
- voices load lazily (getVoices empty = not ready), OS default is often worst voice, ordered preference list as taste
- speech recognition error taxonomy mapped to small named set with a total default mapping

### Existing host-page-adaptation local pack covers:
- quarantine host DOM knowledge in one module (page-adapter/), one file for all selectors
- identify host UI by a net (class families, attribute/role hooks, text/shape fallback), visibility is part of identity
- selectors.js carries provenance (date verified, negative findings)
- a probe entry point that never throws, collects a row per selector
- fixture mirrors host page for CI; manual-test doc for what only live host answers
- never trust a write — verify by re-reading, poll don't sync-check, aim events at app's own DOM subtree
- synthetic keystrokes need keyCode/which/charCode fields (deprecated fields still read by legacy handlers), built in one helper
- put back borrowed host state (pencil mode), degrade gracefully when state unreadable
- host lifecycle: idle timers (nudge with bare Shift keydown/keyup), veils blank content (check overlay before diffing), pre-content splashes
- inert when off: watchers on-demand, MutationObserver disconnects the moment it finds its target

## What to report back (your final answer)

For each genuine candidate that is NOT already covered above: a 1-2 sentence description of the friction, the concrete durable fix it converts to, and the evidence (quote a short phrase, cite approximate timestamps for wall-time claims, note whether this session even has an associated issue — it's issue #201 here so it does).

If nothing clears the bar, say so plainly — that's a fine and common outcome, do not stretch to manufacture a finding. Keep your final report under 500 words.

# Dedup local packs against the canon

The **method** of the growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile a repo's own **local packs**
(`.claudinite/local/packs/`; legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
window) against the shared canon it consumes, pruning local items the canon now covers. Two
callers share it: the unattended [growth-dedup task](../../tasks/growth-dedup/task.md) (which
frames the run — dispatch, the human-gated PR, tracking issue), and an owner asking in-session
to reconcile local packs against the canon. Often there's nothing to prune, and that's fine.

**The yardstick is the mounted canon** — the exact revision the repo currently consumes, what
`.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp — never a live fetch (a promotion is visible
here only once baselining has converged the mount to include it). The mount is never a prune
*target*, only what you prune *against*.

## The three actions — every one removes portable text

- **Remove** a now-duplicated local item, since the canon is the single source of truth for
  portable rules.
- **Strip** a *partially* covered item down to its residue — when an item's general half is now
  canon-owned but it still carries a stronger point about a narrower case, **delete the portable
  half in place and keep only the residue**. A strip is a **deletion that shrinks the entry**:
  lead with the residual point (using the file's own `(canon)` tag convention if it has one),
  never with a meta-line like "this rule is portable (canon)", and **never re-state the
  now-canon rule, its fix, or which pack owns it** — carrying it is exactly what you are
  removing. If your "strip" adds words or restates the canon, you have *un*-deduped the item:
  keep the pre-edit text instead.
- **Rephrase** a local procedure *only* when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed,
  so the local packs stay consistent with the canon they point at — a rephrase tracks a wording
  drift; it never grows the entry and never re-imports canon prose.

An edit that leaves an entry the same size or larger, re-quotes the now-canon rule, or names the
owning pack's fix is a **corruption, not a dedup**. When in doubt about a kept item, leave it
byte-for-byte unchanged rather than "reconcile" its wording. The `dedup-prune-integrity` check
([dedup-integrity.mjs](../../dedup-integrity.mjs)) is the machine backstop: it reds the session
when a dedup-labeled commit grows a local-pack prose file, or when any change adds a line that
restates a canon rule.

## The keep-test: says *more*, not merely says it more specifically

Every local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test.
Distinguish two cases:

- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's
  classes, files, or names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only
  illustration: prune it.
- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule
  leaves out: a tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower
  situation. Keep it.

So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the
general point, or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.

## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose

The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when
a canon check *enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every
session and CI pass. Consult the machine-readable rule catalog
(`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`: id, severity, description,
doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose corpus, and
when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line.
This cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the
same rule — prune the local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd
prune a duplicated prose line. The keep-test above is unchanged.

## Discipline

- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon
  line (or the covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a
  real local lesson.
- **Write only inside the local packs.** A dedup run's whole surface is
  `.claudinite/local/packs/` — never the canon it prunes against, never the project's own code. The
  `growth-write-scope` check ([growth-write-scope.mjs](../../growth-write-scope.mjs)) keys on the
  run's pinned `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs` title and reds any path outside that surface.
- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green
  before delivering.

input.title: Recurring vitest cold-start timeout in visual-snapshots.test.js (help-page)
input.body:
`dev/requirements/ui/visual-snapshots.test.js`'s `help-page` case has intermittently exceeded vitest's default 5000ms test timeout — `Test timed out in 5000ms` — across at least 5 independent sessions over the last two weeks (2026-08-07 ×2, 08-09, 08-10, 08-13), most recently re-diagnosed again in the 2026-08-16 `growth-extract` run (issue #198). It hasn't reproduced in every run (didn't reproduce just now either), which is consistent with it being a cold-start timing issue rather than a deterministic failure.

**Root cause**: `dev/requirements/ui/render/page-to-png.js`'s `pageToPng`/`contentToPng` each call `chromium.launch()` fresh per case (no shared/warm browser instance), and `vitest.config.js` sets no `testTimeout` — so the suite runs on vitest's 5000ms default, which a cold Chromium launch can exceed on a colder container/CI runner.

**Fix**: either set an explicit `testTimeout` in `vitest.config.js` long enough to cover a cold `chromium.launch()`, or launch once and share the browser across the render-heavy cases. `dev/procedures/testing.md` already documents a sibling first-run trap (the `npm ci`-before-`npx vitest` gotcha) and would be a natural place to also note this one if the fix is a config bump rather than a code change.

This has cost repeat diagnostic time across several growth-extract/scheduled sessions without ever landing a fix, because each of those sessions is scoped to writing only this repo's `.claudinite/local/packs/` — outside that scope for an actual `vitest.config.js`/testing.md change. Opening this so it's tracked as a real, actionable item rather than re-discovered indefinitely.
